identity.description:
Show the full text of board entries and scroll the board pane

## Summary

The orchestrator board pane now shows the whole text of each item that needs you, and of its recommendation: long text wraps onto more lines instead of being cut at the right edge. When the board is longer than the pane, the pane shows one page of it with a dim line at the top or bottom that says how many lines are out of view. Type `u`, `d`, `t` or `b` and Enter in the `Row` input to go up a page, down a page, to the top or to the bottom. A row number and Enter still brings that implementer's tab to the front.

**Ticket:** N/A
**Type:** Bug fix

<details><summary>spec.md</summary>

# Spec: board-full-text

The board pane is the mod `hooks/orch-board.tsx`, opened by `/orch-board`. Its tests are `tests/orch-board.test.tsx`. `skills/orchestrator/references/orchestrator-record.md`'s "The board" owns the board JSON; this work does not change the JSON.

## What the pane does now (the cause)

- Every cell of the pane is `Text wrap="truncate"`, cut by `fit()` to its column. A `Needs you` text and its `Recommended:` line are cut at the right edge.
- The pane draws the whole board as one tree. The engine owns the window over a pane body: the person scrolls it with the arrow, page and Home/End keys while the pane has focus, or with the wheel (`ui.scroll`). But the `Row` `Input` has `autoFocus`, so the pane opens with the focus ring on the input, where Up and Down walk the input and then move the ring, and the engine keeps the focused element in view. The window stays at the bottom of the tree, and the top of the board is out of reach. The engine API types are in `/Users/jerridan/.claude/crew/gh-155-orchestrator-board-pane-b7d1/plugin-authoring-ref/types/claude-code.d.ts` (`Pane` props at about line 12985, `SiteScroll` at about 15050, `ui.scroll` event at about 4898 and `UiScrollInput` at about 18427, `$.ui.scroll` at about 2899, `Input` `autoFocus` and `rows` at about 6525).

## Requirements

R1. Full text of an entry. The pane shows every character of each `Needs you` entry's `text`, and of its `Recommended: <recommend>` line, at every width the pane supports (24 columns and up). A text longer than its room continues on the next lines of the pane. No line of the pane is wider than `bodyColumns`.
  - The break rule: a line breaks at the last space that fits; a word longer than the room breaks at the column. A continued line starts under the first character of the text column. Where the text column has fewer than `MIN_QUESTION` (15) cells of room, the text starts on the next line instead, indented by `2 * INDENT`, and wraps there.
  - Acceptance: a test with an entry `text` and a `recommend` each longer than 3 times the pane width, at 24, 40, 60, 80 and 200 columns, joins the drawn lines of that entry, removes all whitespace from them and from the expected text, and finds the whole text and the whole recommendation. It finds no drawn line wider than the columns. This test fails on the current main.

R2. Every line in reach. When the board has more lines than the pane body shows (`props.scroll.bodyRows`), the person can bring every line of the board into view, and the `Row` input stays usable.
  - The mechanism: the mod draws its own window. The tree it returns is at most `bodyRows` lines: a window over the board lines, then the lines pinned at the bottom (the `Row` input, its result line, the footer). The mod keeps the window's first line in module memory of the load, not in `$.state`, so the atom `shape` tag does not change; a reload starts at the top. Each drawn line is one row: the mod wraps text itself (R1) and every `Text` truncates, so its line count is exact.
  - The keys: in the `Row` input, `u` and Enter moves the window up one page, `d` and Enter down one page, `t` and Enter to the top, `b` and Enter to the bottom. These need only typing, so they work while the input has the focus and in any terminal, Herdr included. The mod also hooks `ui.scroll` for its pane: a wheel tick, an arrow or a page key that the engine raises moves the mod's window by `e.by`, and the hook does not call `next`, as the `ui.scroll` doc says for a hook that draws its own rows.
  - A mark: when lines are above the window, its first line is a dim mark that names how many and the key (for example `↑ 12 more · u`); when lines are below, its last line names how many and the key (`↓ 30 more · d`). With the whole board in the window, no mark shows.
  - Acceptance: a test with a board of more lines than `bodyRows` (for example `bodyRows` 10 and 30 rows) submits `d` until the window reaches the end, and every board line (each `Needs you` line, each section title, each row) is drawn in at least one view, and no view draws more than `bodyRows` lines. Then `t` brings the first board line back. This test fails on the current main.
  - Acceptance: a test checks the marks at the top (only the lower mark), in the middle (both), at the end (only the upper mark), and on a board that fits (neither). This test fails on the current main.

R3. The focus key. A row number and Enter in the `Row` input still runs `launcher.py focus <launch_tab>` for that row, for a row out of the view too.
  - Acceptance: the existing R9 tests pass; a new test focuses a row that is out of the current view. This new test is a regression guard and passes on the current main too, because main focuses any row by its number; the charter's item (3) says "still runs", which reads as a guard, not as a new failure.

R4. Narrow widths. At 24, 40 and 60 columns each row of a section keeps its row number, and the column rules of `layout()` (what drops below `NARROW`, what shrinks first) are unchanged for the item rows.
  - Acceptance: the existing R11 tests pass, changed only where they assert the truncation this work removes from a `Needs you` text or recommendation.

R5. The rest of the pane is unchanged: the poll, the toasts, the links, the error and missing-name lines, the R16 match with the text view at 200 columns.
  - Acceptance: every other existing test passes unchanged.

R6. The README section "See an orchestrator's board" tells the person how to scroll the pane.
  - Checklist: the section names `u`, `d`, `t` and `b` with Enter in the `Row` input, says that long text wraps, and follows `.claude/rules/readme.md` (no citation, no design reasoning).

## Global constraints

- Only `hooks/orch-board.tsx`, `tests/orch-board.test.tsx`, `tests/fixtures/` (only if a new fixture is needed) and `README.md` change. The board JSON, `crew-orch.py` and `types/index.d.ts` change only if a stored scroll value needs a field of `OrchBoardView`; if it does, bump the atom `shape` tag as the comment above `view` says.
- The person's terminal is the Herdr app. The `Row` input words of R2 are the way that must work there; the `ui.scroll` hook is a second way and its keys may not reach the pane in every terminal.
- The mod reads no file and writes no file (test R12).
- `claude plugin test`, run with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set to a new empty directory, passes.
- The prose follows ASD-STE100 and `skills/project-lead/references/writing-standard.md`'s "Writing for a person" (README) and `.claude/rules/readme.md`.
- Do not bump the plugin version and do not add a `docs/design.md` §15 number: the orchestrator assigns both.

## Non-goals

- The text view, `crew-orch.py board`.
- Wrapping the text of an item row in a group or the single items: it keeps its truncation by `layout()`.
- A change to what the board JSON holds.
